_about: The map proper: a DJ-202 control name (from controllers/roland-dj-202.json, captured
off the device) bound to a CDJ action (from cdj_actions.py, read off the
firmware's own key table). No MIDI numbers live here -- that is the point
of the split. Re-learning the device changes controllers/roland-dj-202.json and this
'deck' is either a deck id from 'decks' below, or 'focus', meaning the
deck the LOAD buttons last pointed at. Browse is a single shared UI on a
real CDJ pair too -- you browse on the deck you are about to load.

decks._note: deck id -> the tag its machine runs under, i.e. its key socket

bindings._note_load: LOAD does not load here -- on a CDJ the rotary push loads. LOAD picks which deck the browse knob drives.
bindings._note_pads: The CDJ has panel keys the DJ-202 has no button for, so each deck's pads become that deck's panel: 1-4 navigate, 5-8 move within the track. Every one is a key the firmware's own table names, so a pad that does nothing means the deck ignored it, not that the map guessed.
bindings._note_pad78_deck1: Deck 1 pads 7-8 carry the two controls whose effect shows on the screen at once: TempoRange cycles the +/-10 -> +/-16 badge and MasterTempo lights a red MT. Deck 2 keeps scan on 7-8.
bindings._note_jog: The platter's ticks drive JogMov + JogRoundFwd as levels, re-armed while it turns; the platter's touch sensor holds JogTouch on its own so a resting hand does not claim motion.
bindings._note_jog_mode: FX TAP toggles the NXS2's JOG MODE (VINYL/CDJ, report 0x15 bit 0x01). Only in VINYL mode does touching the platter top hold and scratch.
bindings._note_keylock: KEY LOCK is what the NXS2 calls MASTER TEMPO, and the DJ-202's SLIP is the NXS2's SLIP -- both firmware-table keys.

leds._note: role -> control name; midi/leds.py says what each role shows. 'beat' is four LEDs in bar order. 'ring' is the NXS2's jog ring light on the headphone CUE buttons, the only lit DJ-202 buttons with no CDJ function (the deck switch's LED is the pad layer and cannot be used).

_unmapped: The jog is three separate report bits (touch, direction, movement), not a
wheel position, so turning a platter into them is its own job. The DJ-202
jog also sends pitchwheel, which the bridge does not decode yet.
The mixer (faders, EQ, filter, crossfader, cue) has no CDJ target by
design: on real hardware it is a DJM, a separate box. It belongs in an
audio mixer on the host side, not in a panel-key datagram.
